facts.text: The study added 4.2 at.% Cr, designated HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5, to the HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
The Cr-containing alloy was prepared by vacuum arc melting, matching the preparation method used for the Cr-free comparator.
Mechanical performance was evaluated by compression testing at room temperature.
The Cr-containing alloy had a measured secondary-phase volume fraction of 3.8%, approximately 4 vol.%.
Cr addition produced a complex multicomponent Laves phase identified as Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) within the BCC matrix.
The Laves phase formed a reticulated, interconnected network rather than isolated discrete particles.
Cr addition contracted the BCC lattice parameter from approximately 3.392 Å to 3.325 Å.
Severe lattice distortion and increased dislocation density associated with Cr incorporation produced solid-solution hardening.
The reticulated Laves-phase network hindered crack propagation and compensated for the plasticity loss normally associated with a brittle intermetallic phase.
Relative to the Cr-free baseline, Cr addition concurrently increased both yield strength and fracture strain.
Yield strength increased by approximately 13.5%, reaching 1750.6 MPa.
Fracture strain increased by approximately 20.6%, reaching 14.0%.
